reason: The text demonstrates collaboration between leaders and people in multiple instances: (1) Eli and young Samuel work together as Eli helps Samuel understand God's calling, showing mentorship and guidance; (2) More significantly, in the battle narrative, the elders of Israel (leaders) and the people (הָעָם) explicitly consult together when they ask 'why has the Lord defeated us today?', collectively decide to bring the Ark of the Covenant from Shiloh ('נִקְחָה אֵלֵינוּ מִשִּׁלֹה אֶת־ אֲרוֹן בְּרִית יְהוָה'), and jointly execute this strategic decision. The phrase 'וַיִּשְׁלַח הָעָם שִׁלֹה וַיִּשְׂאוּ מִשָּׁם' shows the people sending and collectively carrying out the leadership's decision. While this collaboration ultimately fails in its military objective, the collaborative process itself is clearly present in the narrative.
